ShouldDisappearFromDoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 4 says to think about this one rather than reflex-waive it, so it was traced: ShouldDisappearFromDoom has exactly ONE reader in the whole game, DoomPower.cs:90, and that read is inside `PlayVfx` -- it computes a bool that is passed to StartDoomAnim and to NDoomVfx.Create as the 'should the sprite vanish' flag (DoomPower.cs:80-144). The actual lethality is DoomKill, which does not consult it. So `!Creature.HasPower<SteamEruptionPower>()` (WaterfallGiant.cs:84) only decides whether the Doom animation makes the giant disappear. Presentation. (Doom is additionally Necrobinder content and the sim implements no Doom at all -- `grep -rin doom sts2_rl/` returns nothing -- but the waiver rests on the presentation finding, not on that dormancy.)

AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2, copied verbatim in substance: the sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation IS construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (waterfall_giant.py:36-40). The game runs it from MonsterModel.AfterAddedToRoom awaited by CombatManager.AfterCreatureAdded (CombatManager.cs:860-867) inside StartCombatInternal (CombatManager.cs:393-398), i.e. after every creature is on the board and before Hook.BeforeCombatStart. Same observable today on all three of section 2's clauses (listener set / HP-roll inversion / roll ordering); the concrete trigger that would make it a gap is a relic, potion or power listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. Rule 7: the four relic files and sts2_rl/powers.py that section 2's clause (a)/(b) argument cites are NOT hashed by this record. Here the mechanical content is one field seed, `CurrentPressureGunDamage = BasePressureGunDamage` (WaterfallGiant.cs:159-164, non-ascension 20) -> `self._pressure_gun_dmg = 20` at construction; the rest of the override is SfxCmd.PlayLoop. No power is applied here, so section 2's listener-set clause is vacuous, and the field is a literal that reads no HP.

AfterDeath.rationale: One of monster_state_machine boundary-hole 5's eleven unclaimed overrides. Read to the end (N6): WaterfallGiant.cs:166-179 is two early returns (not my creature / still holding SteamEruptionPower) and then exactly two statements -- `NRunMusicController...UpdateMusicParameter("waterfall_giant_progress", 5f)` and `StopAmbientSfx()`, the latter being SfxCmd.StopLoop (:186-189). A music parameter and an SFX loop stop: entirely presentation, no mechanical behaviour for the sim to be missing. hook_dispatch G5 is not re-verdicted.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node identical to WaterfallGiant.cs:191-222: eight MoveStates, no branch state, initial PRESSURIZE, main ring PRESSURIZE -> STOMP -> RAM -> SIPHON -> PRESSURE_GUN -> PRESSURE_UP -> STOMP (note PRESSURE_UP returns to STOMP, not to PRESSURIZE, on both sides), plus the detached death branch ABOUT_TO_BLOW -> EXPLODE -> EXPLODE (self-loop). ABOUT_TO_BLOW_MOVE carries MustPerformOnceBeforeTransitioning = true on both sides (WaterfallGiant.cs:200-203 vs waterfall_giant.py:69-72). PRESSURE_GUN's and EXPLODE's intents are lambdas over the live damage fields on both sides (:198, :204 vs :61-62, :75-76). Executed (monster_probes_b04.py graphs).

TriggerAboutToBlowState.rationale: C# (WaterfallGiant.cs:301-313): set IsAboutToBlow, play SFX, `CreatureCmd.SetMaxAndCurrentHp(Creature, 999999999m)`, set the infinite HP display, then `SetMoveImmediate(AboutToBlowState, forceTransition: true)`. The sim splits it: the monster sets the flag and does machine.force_current_state(ABOUT_TO_BLOW) + _current_move, and the 999999999 assignment happens one hook later in SteamEruptionPower.on_damage_received. Two sub-points, both checked. (a) forceTransition: true means C#'s SetMoveImmediate SKIPS its NextMove.CanTransitionAway guard (MonsterModel.cs:420-432), so the sim's unguarded force_current_state is the correct analogue here -- monster_state_machine G5's second clause (the missing CanTransitionAway guard) names WaterfallGiant as a trigger, but the trigger does not fire, because this is the forced overload. G5 is not re-verdicted. (b) executed end to end (monster_probes_b04.py giant-blow): a 9999 killing blow leaves hp = max_hp = 999999999, is_about_to_blow True and the move parked on ABOUT_TO_BLOW_MOVE; the next enemy side banks steam_dmg = 30 and removes the power; the one after deals 30 and kills the giant. The sim's extra `if self.is_about_to_blow: return` re-entry guard (waterfall_giant.py:96-97) has no C# counterpart but is unreachable a second time, because SteamEruptionPower is what calls it and the power is removed before EXPLODE.

guards.what: killing the giant fires no on_death in the sim
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-28: SteamEruptionPower is no longer ported onto `should_die`. powers.py:2115-2152 now implements should_remove_from_combat_after_death (`creature is not self.owner`, SteamEruptionPower.cs:28-35), should_stop_combat_from_ending (:23-26) and should_power_be_removed_after_owner_death (:37-40), and hangs the ABOUT_TO_BLOW trigger on `on_death(creature, was_removal_prevented)` guarded by `if was_removal_prevented or creature is not self.owner: return` -- the shape of SteamEruptionPower.cs:15-21, which overrides no ShouldDie. cmds.py:30-65's `_resolve_death` now mirrors CreatureCmd.KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition's two arms (CreatureCmd.cs:506-570) and dispatches Hook.AfterDeath on both. EXECUTED with a spy on a real WATERFALL_GIANT_BOSS combat, giant holding SteamEruption 30 and a player-applied Vulnerable 3: the killing blow fires on_death exactly once with was_removal_prevented=False at hp=0, retained_after_death=True, the corpse is stripped of Vulnerable and keeps SteamEruption (the port of Creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath, Creature.cs:668-671), and the move is forced to ABOUT_TO_BLOW_MOVE. So every on_death listener -- Gremlin Horn included -- now gets the trigger the game gives it. WAS: `should_die` vetoed the death, so hooks.on_death never ran for that blow and the sim fired it once per fight where the game fires twice.

guards.what: SIPHON heal, and its multiplayer factor
guards.rationale: WaterfallGiant.cs:263-270 heals `SiphonHeal * CombatState.Players.Count`; SiphonHeal is the non-ascension 10 (:72). With the sim's single player the factor is 1, so `CreatureCmd.heal(hooks, self, 10)` (waterfall_giant.py:122-125) is the same number. Multiplayer plumbing is noted in the mapping, not treated as a divergence (PROMPT.md scope).

Non-ascension, WaterfallGiant.cs:72-86: PressurizeAmount 15, StompDamage 15, RamDamage 10, PressureUpDamage 13, BasePressureGunDamage 20, PressureGunIncrease 5, SiphonHeal 10; every move except PRESSURIZE also applies SteamEruptionPower 3m (:238, :249, :259, :268, :279) while PRESSURIZE applies the flat 15 (:228). Sim waterfall_giant.py:13-21 = 15 / 3 / 15 / 1 / 10 / 10 / 20 / 5 / 13, and _pressurize (:108-109) grants only the 15. STOMP applies Weak 1 (:248) then Steam 3 -- same order in _stomp (:111-116). PRESSURE_GUN increments its own damage AFTER the attack on both sides (:274-278 vs :128-129), so the first shot is 20 and the second 25; executed in giant-blow, where six sides bank steam=30 (15 + 5x3).

guards.what: ABOUT_TO_BLOW banks the Steam amount then removes the power
guards.rationale: WaterfallGiant.cs:283-289: SteamEruptionDamage = GetPowerAmount<SteamEruptionPower>(), then PowerCmd.Remove, then the presentation-only PressureBuildupIdx = 6 / IncrementBuildUpAnimationTrack. Sim _about_to_blow (waterfall_giant.py:136-140) reads the amount and removes the power in the same order; EXPLODE then attacks for the banked number and calls CreatureCmd.kill on itself (:142-145 vs :291-299). Executed: steam_dmg = 30, powers empty after the ABOUT_TO_BLOW turn, 30 damage on the next.

Presentation only (SHARED-FINDINGS section 4; monster_state_machine N2/N5). The sim models no audio, animation, spine skins, asset preloading or Bestiary, so there is nothing mechanical to port. IncrementBuildUpAnimationTrack (WaterfallGiant.cs:315-329) is wholly inside `if (TestMode.IsOff)` and its whole body is a music parameter, an SFX parameter and a SpineAnimation track. PROMPT.md class 18 was applied: the shipping arm is the IsOff one (TestMode.TurnOnInternal has no caller), so the counter does advance in a real run -- but its only readers are ShouldFadeAfterDeath (:157) and the animation track, both presentation. Nothing mechanical depends on it, which is why the sim carries no counterpart.

guards.issue: Closed 2026-08-02: waterfall_giant.py:85-87 now constructs `lambda: Intent(MoveType.DEATH_BLOW, damage=self._steam_eruption_dmg, also=(MoveType.ATTACK,))`. WAS: `also` was empty. Same class as `monster/living_fog`'s sibling guard: `DeathBlowIntent` (game src\Core\MonsterMoves\Intents\DeathBlowIntent.cs:10) is a `SingleAttackIntent` : `AttackIntent`, but its `IntentType` override is `IntentType.DeathBlow` (:16), not `.Attack`; `MonsterModel.IntendsToAttack` (MonsterModel.cs:241-245) explicitly ORs the two IntentTypes together, and that predicate gates `GoForTheEyes.OnPlay`'s Weak application and glow-gold targeting hint (GoForTheEyes.cs:22-27,49-52). `NIntent.cs:135`'s `intent is AttackIntent` check also renders EXPLODE_MOVE's damage number like any other attack, by C# class hierarchy rather than the enum. Before the fix, Go For The Eyes into an about-to-EXPLODE giant never applied Weak, and the observation's attack flag / damage preview for EXPLODE_MOVE were blank. Found by an RL task, not by this record's original audit (which verdicted GenerateMoveStateMachine faithful without checking `also=` against `MonsterModel.IntendsToAttack`).
guards.rationale: EXECUTED: `test/test_combat_obs_v4.py` gained a real Waterfall Giant encounter test driving it to EXPLODE_MOVE and asserting the observation's attack flag/damage preview are populated; full suite green at 4399 passed / 6 xfailed / 0 failed after the fix. Confirmed independently by reading `DeathBlowIntent.cs`, `SingleAttackIntent.cs`, `AttackIntent.cs`, `MonsterModel.cs:241-245`, `GoForTheEyes.cs:22-27,49-52` and `NIntent.cs:135` in the game source, and `waterfall_giant.py:73-88` in the sim, on 2026-08-02. **Sweep for further sites of the same class, EXECUTED 2026-08-02**: `grep -rn "DeathBlow" --include=*.cs` over the whole game source finds exactly two `new DeathBlowIntent(` call sites in the entire game -- `src\Core\Models\Monsters\GasBomb.cs:62` and `src\Core\Models\Monsters\WaterfallGiant.cs:204` -- matching the sim's exactly two `Intent(MoveType.DEATH_BLOW, ...)` sites (`grep -rn "MoveType.DEATH_BLOW" sts2_rl/monsters`: living_fog.py and waterfall_giant.py only), both now fixed. Widened further: `grep -rn "IntentType\." --include=*.cs src` excluding the Intents directory's own class declarations returns exactly one hit in the whole game -- `MonsterModel.cs:244`'s `IntendsToAttack` -- so `IntendsToAttack` is the ONLY predicate anywhere in the game that composes two distinct `IntentType` enum values; there is no second OR-of-intent-types predicate to miss. Separately, `grep -n "class .*Intent"` over `src\Core\MonsterMoves\Intents\` shows `DeathBlowIntent : SingleAttackIntent : AttackIntent` is the ONLY intent subclass in the game that inherits through another concrete intent type rather than descending directly from `AbstractIntent` (`MultiAttackIntent`/`SingleAttackIntent` also extend `AttackIntent`, but their own `IntentType` is already `.Attack`, so the sim's plain `MoveType.ATTACK` already covers them with no `also=` needed) -- confirmed via `grep -rn "is AttackIntent\|is StatusIntent" --include=*.cs src`, which finds only `NIntent.cs:135`'s single dual check. Conclusion: DeathBlow was not one instance of a wider undetected class -- it IS the whole class, both of its two instances are now fixed, and there is no third `also=`-composition predicate in the game for anything else in `sts2_rl/monsters/**` to have missed. Found none, not merely did-not-look.
